paper-sleepsynth-evaluating-use-syntheti.needs: Full text not obtained; affiliations and exact venue name could not be confirmed from the abstract-tier evidence.

paper-steel-strip-defect-sample-2023.summary: This paper proposes SDE-ConSinGAN, a single-image GAN-based model for generating synthetic steel strip surface defect images to address data scarcity in industrial defect classification, using image-feature cutting and splicing plus a channel attention mechanism to improve sample diversity and reduce training time. The CTGAN paper is cited only in passing in the introduction, mischaracterized as proposing conditional GANs generally, with no SDV-family code, model, or concept actually used in the work.
paper-steel-strip-defect-sample-2023.needs: Citation appears to misattribute CTGAN as a general CGAN proposal; no SDV-family term appears in the body text outside the reference list.

paper-trgan-transactions-2023.summary: Generates synthetic bank transactions with a supervisor-controlled GAN whose conditional vector encodes both client categories and chronology, and draws inter-transaction intervals from Poisson variables with per-client intensities calibrated by optimisation. SDV's RDT transformers do the preprocessing the model depends on, the frequency encoder for high-cardinality client fields and the Gaussian normalizer for numeric ones, and CTGAN and CopulaGAN are two of the three models the result is measured against.

paper-autonomous-cybersecurity-automl-20.summary: Proposes an AutoML framework for intrusion detection in zero-touch mobile networks, automating the pipeline steps a human analyst would otherwise tune. TVAE is the automated data-balancing stage inside that pipeline, so SDV's autoencoder synthesizer runs as a component of an autonomous system rather than as an object of study.

paper-mia-tabular-synthesis-2022.summary: Attacks four tabular synthesizers to see whether an attacker can tell which records trained them, under both black-box and white-box access, then tests whether differentially private training defends them. CTGAN is one of the four victim models trained and attacked, and had to be modified to a Wasserstein loss because its gradient penalty resists DP training.

paper-assessment-creditworthiness-models.summary: This paper presents a methodology for training credit-scoring (behavioral scoring) models on synthetic data and evaluating their performance when applied to real-world financial data, finding a modest AUC/KS drop relative to models trained on real data. The authors generate synthetic borrower datasets using CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers under different architectures and feature sets, evaluating fidelity with CSTest, KSTest, and logistic detection. SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) v5.0.0 is explicitly used as the Python implementation for synthetic data generation, running its CTGAN and TVAE synthesizers as the core generators underpinning the entire empirical study.

paper-imbalanced-classification-knn-gene.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid intrusion-detection method combining a KNN-based sampling strategy with generative adversarial networks to address class imbalance in network traffic data. The GAN component is used to synthesize minority-class samples to improve detection performance on imbalanced intrusion datasets. The work cites the TGAN paper from the SDV family, apparently as related prior art on GAN-based tabular data generation.
paper-imbalanced-classification-knn-gene.needs: Only metadata available; no abstract or full text obtained, so it is unclear whether TGAN/CTGAN code was actually run or only cited in passing. Cannot confirm integration mechanism beyond citation.

paper-prediction-ultimate-condition-frp-.summary: This paper proposes a hybrid gradient-boosting model to predict the ultimate condition (strain/strength) of FRP-confined recycled aggregate concrete, addressing the scarcity of experimental data in this domain. The authors enrich their small training dataset using a tabular generative adversarial network before fitting the boosting model. The tabular GAN, cited to the TGAN paper, is used as a data-augmentation generator to expand the training set for the prediction model.
paper-prediction-ultimate-condition-frp-.needs: Full text not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN/sdv-dev code was run directly (api_user), reimplemented (port), or merely cited as motivation. Integration and importance are best estimates from title/metadata only.

paper-privacy-preserving-synthetic-educa.summary: This paper presents a generative modeling and evaluation framework for producing synthetic educational log data (using Markov chains and neural network-based generators) that preserves participant privacy, and proposes a practical re-identification risk measure to show naive pseudonymization is insufficient. It is evaluated on real massive open educational datasets, showing one method can scale to a million rows in seconds. SDV (sdv.dev) is cited in related work as an example of a Bayesian-network-based synthetic data toolkit, noted as lacking re-identification risk measurement, but it is not run in the experiments.

paper-outlier-benchmark-vine-2021.summary: Builds an outlier-detection benchmark whose synthetic data is realistic rather than simplistic, fitting distributions to real datasets so that generated outliers deviate in characterisable ways. Vine copulas are one of the two fitted distributions and the one that reconstructs outliers best, letting the benchmark test detectors against deviations in the dependency structure rather than in single attributes.

paper-exploiting-script-similarities-com.summary: This paper addresses the scarcity of training data for Tesseract LSTM OCR on Kurdish (Sorani, Persian-Arabic script) by pretraining on an Arabic dataset and fine-tuning with a small amount of Kurdish court-case text and Unikurd fonts, achieving 95.45% accuracy. The Synthetic Data Vault paper is cited only in the reference list with no engagement in the body text.

paper-gans-tabular-healthcare-generation.summary: A survey of GAN architectures adapted for tabular healthcare data, cataloguing roughly twenty models by year, reported utility/privacy metrics, and public repository links, aiming to help institutions choose synthesizers and test them for privacy risk. TGAN and CTGAN appear as two of the surveyed models, each listed with its sdv-dev GitHub repository and the utility metrics reported in their original papers, but neither is run by the authors themselves. SDV's TGAN and CTGAN are cited and described as prior tabular-GAN work within this comparative review, not executed as part of the study.
paper-gans-tabular-healthcare-generation.needs: Full text and citing sentences were not obtained; cannot confirm whether TGAN was merely listed in a survey table or discussed/run experimentally. Judgment based solely on metadata and title.

paper-ensemble-machine-learning-framewor.summary: This paper proposes an ensemble machine-learning framework (XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM) to automatically identify sweet spots in shale reservoirs from well-log data, and explores GAN-based data augmentation to expand small training sets from 73 horizontal wells. Both a conditional GAN and CTGAN are trained to generate synthetic well-log samples, but the resulting synthetic data yields low agreement rates (27.44% and 68.58% respectively) compared with real data, leading the authors to favor the gradient-boosting ensemble instead. CTGAN's conditional generator/discriminator architecture is run as one of two GAN-based data-augmentation baselines that are ultimately found unsuitable for this oilfield dataset.
paper-ensemble-machine-learning-framewor.needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether authors used the sdv-dev CTGAN package or their own reimplementation of its architecture, since only 'specific structures of the CTGAN generator and discriminator' are mentioned without library/package naming.

paper-clustering-methodology-mixed-sets-.summary: This conference paper proposes a methodology for clustering mixed (numerical and categorical) data sets without a labeled variable, applying it to a case study of safe houses used in kidnapping crimes drawn from official surveys. The work develops its own clustering pipeline and evaluation metrics rather than generating synthetic data. The original SDV (Synthetic Data Vault) paper by Patki et al. is only listed in the reference list, with no engagement in the body text.
paper-clustering-methodology-mixed-sets-.needs: Full text and abstract were not obtained; cannot confirm whether SDV is discussed, used, or merely listed in references.

paper-privacy-preserving-synthetic-healt.summary: This work investigates using GAN-generated synthetic medical data for teaching data science in health informatics, addressing the restricted access to real electronic health records under privacy laws like HIPAA. The authors propose a novel Wasserstein GAN trained in a secure environment and benchmark it against five other generative approaches on MIMIC-III mortality data using nearest-neighbor adversarial-accuracy metrics for utility and privacy. One of the comparison baselines, 'Gaussian Multivariate', is cited to the SDV paper, representing SDV's Gaussian Copula synthesizer run as one of several generative methods evaluated.
paper-privacy-preserving-synthetic-healt.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV's actual Gaussian Copula implementation (library) was run or only its statistical method was reimplemented.

paper-pareto-optimal-mechanism-demand-20.summary: This paper proposes a Pareto optimal mechanism for demand-side platforms operating in real-time bidding (RTB) online advertising markets, addressing efficiency and fairness in auction-based ad allocation. It appears in Information Sciences and cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, but the nature of that citation cannot be determined from the available metadata.
paper-pareto-optimal-mechanism-demand-20.needs: Full text not obtained; only metadata and a citation link to the SDV DSAA 2016 paper are known. Cannot verify whether SDV is discussed, used, or merely listed in references.

paper-comparing-recommender-systems-synt.summary: This paper proposes SynRec, a data protection framework that generates synthetic user-item recommendation data by replacing or synthesizing values to prevent disclosure of sensitive information while preserving utility for comparing recommender algorithms. It reports preliminary proof-of-concept experiments and outlines future research directions for practical deployment. The SDV paper (Patki et al. 2016) is cited only in a bibliographic list of synthetic data generation categories, with no use of the software.
paper-comparing-recommender-systems-synt.needs: Full text not available; only abstract and citing sentence seen, so cannot confirm whether SDV software/method is used anywhere in the experiments.

paper-synthetic-classification-regressio.summary: This paper proposes a Synthetic Data Approach for Classification and Regression (SDAC/SDAR), which uses probability distribution estimation combined with a k-nearest neighbor model to generate synthetic data for machine learning tasks facing insufficient or privacy-restricted samples. It positions its method against prior approaches including SMOTE and GAN, evaluating on five public datasets for classification and regression. SDV (the Synthetic Data Vault) is cited and described in related work as a relational-database synthesizing approach the authors contrast their method against, but it is not run in the experiments.
paper-synthetic-classification-regressio.needs: Full text not obtained; judgment based on abstract and citing sentences only, which appear in related-work discussion.

paper-active-tabular-augmentation-2026.summary: Argues that distributional fidelity is the wrong objective for augmentation under data scarcity and instead selects what to synthesise by a policy that targets where the current learner is weakest, inpainting the chosen regions with a diffusion model over rounds, and reports gains over augmenters that optimise fidelity alone. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the seven compared augmentation methods, run from their official implementations at the same synthetic budget and data splits as the rest.

preprint-casualsynth-generating-structur.summary: This paper proposes CausalSynth, a framework that decouples causal structure generation (via structural causal models and ancestral sampling) from semantic realization (via an LLM 'realizer'), with an iterative consistency-verification loop to correct violations of imposed causal structure. It is evaluated on three causal benchmarks (ASIA, ALARM, MIMIC-Struct) against LLM prompting, latent-variable generators, diffusion-based tabular generators, and causal-discovery baselines. CTGAN is one of the latent-variable baselines run for comparison against the proposed framework.

preprint-equilibrium-training-energy-mod.summary: The paper introduces Parallel Trajectory Tempering (PTT), a training algorithm for Energy-Based Models that maintains equilibrium sampling throughout training, improving on Persistent Contrastive Divergence for Restricted Boltzmann Machines and other EBMs. On discrete tabular data experiments, the authors report their method surpasses state-of-the-art deep generative models. CTGAN appears only as a citation in the paper's reference list, with no passage in the extracted full text discussing or running it.
preprint-equilibrium-training-energy-mod.needs: Full text extraction found no passage mentioning CTGAN despite it being listed as cited; cannot confirm whether CTGAN was actually run as a baseline for the tabular data experiments or merely cited in the reference list.

preprint-machine-learning-enhanced-non-2.summary: This work proposes a compact shallow-deep neural network (s-DNN) using only FIB-4's five clinical variables to detect advanced liver fibrosis in MASLD patients, comparing it against FIB-4, TabPFN, and fine-tuned GPT-4o across biopsy-confirmed cohorts from China, Malaysia, and India. In its related-work discussion it describes a prior study that used CTGAN-based synthetic tabular data generation combined with CatBoost and feature engineering on the same cohorts to improve external AUROC. CTGAN is only cited and described as prior art, not run in the present study.
preprint-machine-learning-enhanced-non-2.needs: Confirm whether the cited prior study [14] itself used the sdv-dev CTGAN implementation rather than an independent reimplementation; this paper only references it in prose.

preprint-mending-synthetic-healthcare-ma.summary: A preprint proposing MAPS, a model-agnostic post-hoc refinement framework intended to improve the quality of synthetic healthcare data regardless of which generator produced it. The work sits in the healthcare synthetic-data space and cites the original SDV DSAA 2016 paper as background on synthetic data generation. SDV is only cited, not run or benchmarked in the available evidence.
preprint-mending-synthetic-healthcare-ma.needs: Full text not available; cannot confirm whether SDV is run, benchmarked, or merely cited for background in this healthcare synthetic-data refinement paper.

preprint-synthetic-customer-360-benchmar.summary: This preprint introduces a synthetic Customer 360 benchmark for omnichannel retail that generates multi-table customer, household, and transaction data with known ground truth for identity-resolution, data-quality, and golden-record survivorship evaluation, validated across 335 predeclared experimental runs. In its related-work discussion and a comparison table of prior synthetic-data generators, it cites the Synthetic Data Vault as an example of learned relational/multi-table synthesis that lacks task-specific cluster truth or injected-event lineage. SDV's relational multi-table modeling approach is discussed and contrasted with the authors' own benchmark design, but SDV itself is not run.

preprint-what-you-want-theory-2024.summary: This paper presents a rigorous auditing framework for differentially private synthetic data generation (DP-SDG) algorithms, using membership inference attacks in black-box and white-box threat models to empirically verify theoretical DP guarantees and uncover real implementation bugs across six DP-SDG systems. The authors find both known and new DP violations, including one in a DPWGAN implementation submitted to the NIST DP Synthetic Data Challenge. SDV is cited only in passing as one of several software libraries that popularized the distance-to-closest-record (DCR) heuristic, with no SDV code run in the experiments.

paper-openwifi-anonymization-2024.summary: Anonymises OpenWiFi network data before it is forwarded for downstream use, framing anonymization as the operator's obligation rather than the recipient's problem. CTGAN is applied to obscure the actual traffic information, so SDV's generator functions as a disclosure control rather than a data expander.

preprint-inference-attacks-taxonomy-surv.summary: This is a survey that proposes a '3MP' taxonomy for inference attacks against machine learning models in MLaaS settings, reviewing attack types, workflows, and countermeasures across a large literature. It cites GAN-based tabular data synthesis works, including TGAN and CTGAN, only in a bibliographic reference list to support a passing remark that GANs are unsatisfactory for structured data generation, without further engagement. TGAN and CTGAN are mentioned only as citations, never run or otherwise used in the survey.

preprint-mcgan-enhancing-gan-training-20.summary: This paper proposes Monte Carlo GAN (MCGAN), a generic enhancement to GAN training that replaces the standard generative loss with a regression loss reformulating generator training as a least-squares task, and demonstrates gains in stability and quality across image, time series, and video GAN backbones. CTGAN is mentioned only in passing among prior conditional GAN works cited in the introduction, with no experiments run using it.

preprint-evaluation-synthetic-longitudin.summary: This preprint discusses and demonstrates methods for evaluating the quality of synthetic longitudinal electronic health records, covering fidelity via low-dimensional projections, a discriminative goodness-of-fit classifier, utility via train-on-synthetic-test-on-real clinical prediction tasks, and privacy risk via attribute inference. The authors apply these metrics to synthetic EHR data generated from the MIMIC-IV dataset using two open-source libraries. SDV's PARSynthesizer (sequential/longitudinal model) is run alongside Gretel-Synthetics to generate the synthetic longitudinal data that the proposed evaluation metrics are then applied to.

paper-logical-functional-dependencies-20.summary: Introduces the notion of logical dependency between attributes alongside the existing notion of functional dependency, gives a Q-score that quantifies it, and uses that measure to test whether generators reproduce the dependencies present in the real table, concluding that none of the models examined preserves both reliably on small datasets. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the seven generators run and scored, and the study describes CTGAN's mode-specific normalisation, its variational Gaussian mixture mode selection, its conditional vector and its training-by-sampling strategy as the design being tested.

paper-diverse-community-benchmark-2023.summary: Publishes a set of curated excerpts from American Community Survey data, chosen so that privacy algorithms can be tested on small, tractable populations whose subgroup structure is visible, and pairs them with an evaluation suite that surfaces defects aggregate utility scores hide. CTGAN, listed as the SDV implementation, is one of the synthesizers run across the excerpts as the non-differentially-private neural comparator, and the analysis reports it failing to preserve constraints that hold for child records and dropping a housing-feature constraint.

preprint-realistic-synthetic-financial-t.summary: This paper presents an agent-based synthetic financial transaction dataset generator calibrated to real-world payment behavior, releasing several public AML (Anti-Money Laundering) benchmark datasets to compare machine learning models for laundering detection. It argues synthetic data can outperform real data here because ground-truth labels are complete, whereas most real-world laundering goes undetected. SDV is cited only in the reference list among prior synthetic data works, with no evidence it was used in the generator or experiments.

preprint-synthetic-demographic-generatio.summary: This preprint introduces DGGAN, a custom Generative Adversarial Network that generates synthetic individual-level demographic data (age, gender, occupation, etc.) intended to enrich transaction data and improve card fraud detection, tested on an Olympic athletes dataset and a US census income dataset. The authors evaluate their generated data using SDMetrics' KSComplement, TVComplement, CorrelationSimilarity and ContingencySimilarity scores, and separately describe CTGAN's training-by-sampling technique for handling discrete attributes as an idea informing their own generator design. SDMetrics is run directly as the evaluation tool for synthetic-data quality, while CTGAN's conditional training-by-sampling approach is only cited and described, not executed.
preprint-synthetic-demographic-generatio.needs: CTGAN itself is only cited for its training-by-sampling idea, not run as a library; the DGGAN generator is the authors' own architecture, so CTGAN's integration here is citation_only while SDMetrics is the actually-run component.

paper-convgen-oversampling-2022.summary: Argues that deep oversamplers trained adversarially need more data than small imbalanced tables provide, and proposes ConvGeN, which learns convex combinations of minority neighbourhoods so that generated points stay inside the convex space of the minority class and remain separable from the majority. CTGAN is one of the two tabular generators it is measured against: the paper runs it from the sdv-dev repository, describes its conditional vector and packing discriminator, and automates the discrete-versus-continuous column declaration it requires, reporting that on smaller datasets CTGAN performs worse than the non-generative baseline.

preprint-faking-feature-importance-cauti.summary: This paper empirically studies whether feature importance rankings derived from differentially-private synthetic data agree with those from the original data, using PrivBayes and PATE-CTGAN across artificial and real-world datasets. It finds that agreement is inconsistent and degrades under stronger privacy guarantees, cautioning against using DP synthetic data for exploratory feature engineering in sensitive domains like finance and healthcare. CTGAN (Xu et al., 2019) is cited only as the underlying GAN architecture that Rosenblatt et al. (2020) adapted into PATE-CTGAN, which the authors run via the smartnoise-sdk and privgem implementations rather than the SDV package itself.
preprint-faking-feature-importance-cauti.needs: CTGAN itself is not run via the SDV/ctgan package; the actual differentially-private descendant PATE-CTGAN is implemented through smartnoise-sdk and privgem, so CTGAN's role here is purely as cited prior architecture.

thesis-augmenting-high-dimensional-deep-.summary: This master's thesis proposes a framework for augmenting annotated image datasets with deep generative models and a method for quantitatively evaluating the resulting synthetic data quality, applying it to pupil-localization datasets and standard benchmarks. It cites the SDV paper by Patki, Wedge and Veeramachaneni as an example of generative models being used as a drop-in replacement for a relational database in the low-dimensional data setting, without running the system itself.
